Article Title: 'Pellet guns in Delhi, AK-47s in Bihar': Rahul Gandhi attacks Modi govt over 'jaanleva' system against students
Article Text:
Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you perceive a pattern in the way the government addresses student issues across different states? Yes, the response is similar everywhere. No, responses vary significantly. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Monday mounted a fresh attack on PM Narendra Modi-led Centre, alleging that the "entire system is downright deadly against students."His remarks came in the backdrop of over a month-long student agitation that recently concluded following the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister.Referring to reports of alleged police action during a student protest in Bihar, Rahul Gandhi shared a report and said, "News is coming in that AK-47 bullets have been fired at protesting students in Bihar, and hundreds of students have been arrested with FIRs being filed against them."He also questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi , saying, "Mr Modi, where did your promise go that no FIRs would be filed against students and they would be released? Instead, deadly attacks and brutality are being unleashed on them."Rahul also referred to the July 20 students' march to Parliament from Jantar Mantar, during which clashes were reported between protesters and police.He alleged, "In Delhi, pellet guns were fired at students, and in Bihar, AK-47s.Whether it's Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Bihar, or Delhi—the pattern is the same everywhere."Questioning the Modi government's efforts to address irregularities in examinations, Rae Bareli MP said, "I've said it before: this government is dishonest. Real reform is beyond their capability. They'll backtrack on their words and use every trick in the book to suppress students' voices."He added, "Mr Modi, apologize to the country's students. And take action against those who attacked and crushed the students—not against the students themselves."Meanwhile, responding to the Congress' demand that the Prime Minister and the Union home minister apologise over the alleged police action, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra said, "I have heard that FIRs are still being filed against students in Bihar and Bengal. I have heard this, but it is not yet verified. So, what is the use then?"Nearly 200 students, who were allegedly detained following the July 22 and July 25 protests demanding the resignation of former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET paper leak, remained in custody for more than 24 hours at police stations across the city, advocates claimed.Meanwhile, a police personnel in Bihar's Siwan district was suspended for allegedly firing an AK-47 rifle during the violence that broke out during the July 25 bandh.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi mounted a fresh attack on PM Narendra Modi-led Centre. His remarks came in the backdrop of over a month-long student agitation that recently concluded following the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister.

Article Title: DMK demands immediate NEET ban, seeks probe into Jantar Mantar violence
Article Text:
Lok Sabha, Parliament (ANI photo)

NEW DELHI: MK Stalin-led DMK has demanded an immediate ban on the nationwide medical entrance examination NEET.DMK MP TR Baalu on Monday submitted an adjournment motion notice in the Lok Sabha, seeking a ban on NEET in ongoing Monsoon Session.The demand comes in the wake of the NEET UG paper leak in May, which triggered nationwide outrage and over a month of student protests that eventually led to the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.The DMK also demanded an inquiry into the alleged indiscriminate use of lethal weapons against protesting students at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar.On the same day as Pradhan's resignation, the PM Modi-led Centre appointed Pralhad Joshi as the new Union education minister.Pradhan's resignation, however, helped calm the protests after the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which had been leading the agitation, appealed to protesters to return home, saying their primary demand had been met following a meeting with Union ministers Jagat Prakash Nadda and Jitendra Singh.
Article Summary: DMK MP TR Baalu on Monday submitted an adjournment motion notice in the Lok Sabha, seeking a ban on NEET. The demand comes in the wake of the NEET UG paper leak in May, which triggered nationwide outrage and over a month of student protests.

Article Title: 'Govt-ordered probe an eyewash': Tripura Congress MLA demands judicial inquiry into DGP Anurag Dhankar's death
Article Text:
Tripura DGP Anurag Dhankar was found dead in state police headquarters on July 20

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Tripura Congress MLA Sudip Roy Barman on Sunday reiterated the party's demand for a judicial probe into the death of state DGP Anurag Dhankar, who was found dead at the police headquarters in Agartala on July 20."From day one, we have been demanding a judicial probe by a sitting high court judge into the unnatural death of the DGP, keeping in mind the circumstances leading to the recovery of his body," he told a press conference at the Congress Bhavan in Agartala."The condition in which we saw his body at the morgue was as if he was in deep sleep, with no visible wounds that are generally found in such cases. We strongly believe that a team led by an SP-rank officer cannot clear the many doubts surrounding the incident.That is why we want a judicial inquiry into the unnatural death," Roy Barman added.A three-member team headed by West Tripura SP Namit Pathak has been constituted to investigate the matter.Roy Barman termed the Tripura government's decision to investigate the case through a three-member team as an "eyewash." He alleged that the "honest DGP was heckled over some issues days before his death."The Congress MLA also expressed disappointment over the Tripura high court not taking suo motu cognisance of Dhankar's death."The people of the state are also upset over the role of our high court. When the legislature, bureaucracy and media succumb, it is the judiciary that comes out and stands for the cause of people's rights. Unfortunately, we have not seen the high court take any suo motu cognisance in many incidents in the state since former Chief Justice Deepak Kumar Gupta's tenure ended," he said.Dhankar, a native of Uttar Pradesh's Baghpat, was a 1994-batch IPS officer of the Tripura cadre. He took over as the state's DGP in May 2025.The officer had led the CBI probe into the alleged Rs 13,000-crore Punjab National Bank fraud involving diamantaire Nirav Modi and the reinvestigation into the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.
Article Summary: Tripura DGP Anurag Dhankar was found dead at the police headquarters in Agartala on July 20. Tripura Congress MLA Sudip Roy Barman reiterated the party's demand for a judicial probe into the death. A three-member team has been constituted to investigate the matter.

Article Title: Centre ready for NEET debate, opposition should participate, says Haryana CM Nayab Singh Saini
Article Text:
Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini affirmed the Centre's readiness for parliamentary discussion on NEET exam irregularities.





GURGAON : Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini on Saturday said the Centre was prepared for a discussion in Parliament on alleged irregularities in the NEET examination and maintained that those found responsible for any wrongdoing would face strict action.Speaking to reporters after attending a BJP meeting in Gurgaon, Saini said the issue concerned the future of millions of students and reiterated that the government would not spare anyone found guilty of examination-related offences, including paper leaks.“The government is ready for a discussion on the issue in Parliament. The opposition should also participate in the debate and put forward any constructive suggestions,” Saini said, alleging that opposition parties were avoiding a discussion on the matter.He said the government was committed to strengthening the examination system and preventing paper leaks through stricter laws and more effective mechanisms.Referring to concerns over examination integrity, Saini said action had been taken promptly in recent cases and asserted that those involved in compromising the examination process would be dealt with in accordance with the law.The chief minister also criticised the Congress, claiming paper leak incidents had occurred during its tenure and alleging delays in cancelling examinations in some cases. He said the current government had acted swiftly in dealing with such instances.Saini, who is in Gurgaon two-day visit, attended a BJP meeting to discuss year-long programmes planned to mark the 650th birth anniversary of Guru Ravidas.
Article Summary: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini affirmed the Centre's readiness for parliamentary discussion on NEET exam irregularities. He said the issue concerned the future of millions of students and reiterated that the government would not spare anyone found guilty of examination-related offences.

Article Title: Former CM MK Stalin asks CM Vijay to 'open his mouth' on custodial deaths
Article Text:
CM Vijay, former CM MK Stalin





CHENNAI: Former CM MK Stalin on Friday asked when chief minister C Joseph Vijay would "open his mouth" on the continuing custodial deaths.Stalin on X accused the TVK govt of refusing to accept accountability or even apologise."Doesn't the chief minister like the two words- accountability and apology?" Stalin asked.Recalling the remarks of Vijay who questioned before the 2026 assembly election that "is saying sorry enough?" over custodial deaths, Stalin said that after becoming chief minister, Vijay was unwilling even to apologise and questioned where he was "hiding".He also condemned the TVK govt, alleging that it had not even shown the compassion to console the families of those who died in custody.Recently, a youth Arunachalam died allegedly due to custodial death in Tuticorin but police denied it.
Article Summary: Former CM MK Stalin asked when chief minister C Joseph Vijay would "open his mouth" on the continuing custodial deaths. He accused the TVK govt of refusing to accept accountability or even apologise."Doesn't the chief minister like the two words- accountability and apology?" Stalin asked.

Article Title: Man Allegedly Murdered Over Accidental Brush at South Delhi Bus Stand
Article Text:
New Delhi:





A 40-year-old man was arrested for allegedly murdering a 45-year-old man following a trivial verbal altercation after the victim accidentally brushed against him at a bus stand near Safdarjung Hospital in south Delhi Friday night.The deceased was identified as Manoj Singh , a native of Bihar’s Nawada district. He worked with a clothing hawker near Safdarjung Hospital and was the sole breadwinner for his family, comprising his wife and four children.According to police, information about a quarrel near Gate No. 3 of the AIIMS metro station on Aurobindo Marg was received around 10.30 pm.By the time police reached the spot, the accused, identified as 40-year-old Lokesh , a resident of Taimur Nagar in New Friends Colony, had already been overpowered by members of the public and handed over to the police.Manoj was rushed to Safdarjung Hospital where doctors declared him dead during treatment. The body was preserved for a post-mortem examination to ascertain the exact cause of death.A case was registered under Section 103 (murder) of BNS at Hauz Khas police station. The accused was arrested.
Article Summary: Manoj Singh, 45, was the sole breadwinner for his family, comprising his wife and four children. Manoj was rushed to Safdarjung Hospital where doctors declared him dead. The body was preserved for a post-mortem examination to ascertain the exact cause of death.

Article Title: Man held from Rajasthan in Delhi fraud case
Article Text: New Delhi: Investigation into the alleged UPI fraud targeting an east Delhi resident led police to uncover a money trail spanning multiple bank accounts and state borders.Following the digital and financial trail, investigators identified the layer-1 beneficiary, Kailash Saini, who had allegedly received the defrauded money before routing it through multiple bank accounts to conceal the proceeds.The case came to light after a woman lodged a complaint alleging that she had been cheated through a fraudulent UPI transaction. During investigation, police analysed the money trail on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, banking transactions and digital evidence, which led them to the first beneficiary account.“A team tracked and travelled to Saini’s native village in Rajasthan , after tracing his location. He had fled and switched off his mobile phone to evade arrest,” said DCP (East) Rajeev Kumar . He added that cops then relied on local intelligence, field enquiries and technical surveillance before zeroing in on his location in Jaipur, where he was apprehended.The 28-year-old accused was arrested after police found that around Rs 1.2 lakh, allegedly siphoned from the complainant, had been credited to his bank account before being transferred through multiple accounts to obscure the money trail.Police said they seized a mobile phone allegedly used in the offence and two bank passbooks linked to the financial transactions from his possession. The accused was produced before a court and remanded to judicial custody.
Article Summary: The case came to light after a woman lodged a complaint alleging that she had been cheated through a fraudulent UPI transaction. The 28-year-old accused was arrested after police found that around Rs 1.2 lakh, allegedly siphoned from the complainant, had been credited to his bank account before being transferred through multiple accounts.

Article Title: Fire at Byculla police station building in Mumbai; no one hurt
Article Text:
File pic for representation

Mumbai:





A fire broke out on the first floor of the ground-plus-one-storey Byculla police station building on Hansraj Marg in Byculla East on Sunday evening.The incident was reported at 8.24pm. Fire brigade personnel, along with officials from BEST, Mumbai Police and the civic ward office, rushed to the spot to contain the blaze.According to officials, the fire was confined to the first floor of the police station. No injuries were reported.The cause of the fire was not immediately known.Confirming the incident, deputy police commissioner Jayant Meena said, “Yes, there has been a fire incident in Byculla police station building. It has been doused by the fire brigade. Prima facie it was caused by a short circuit. Further necessary action is being taken.“
Article Summary: Fire broke out on the first floor of the ground-plus-one-storey Byculla police station building on Hansraj Marg on Sunday evening. Fire brigade personnel, along with officials from BEST, Mumbai Police and the civic ward office rushed to the spot to contain the blaze.

Article Title: Congress stages rasta roko in Kalyan over police action on Jantar Mantar protesters
Article Text:
Congress workers staged a protest in Kalyan West against alleged police action.





KALYAN: Congress workers staged a rasta roko protest at Shivaji Chowk in Kalyan West to protest against the alleged police action on students demonstrating at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi over the alleged paper leak issue.Led by Navin Singh, Kalyan District President, the protesters raised slogans against the Centre and demanded action over the alleged assault on students and peaceful demonstrators by the Delhi Police.Traffic was briefly affected in the area before police intervened.The party also submitted a memorandum to the Kalyan tehsildar, addressed to the President of India, seeking an inquiry into the alleged police action against students and Congress leaders, including Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other party leaders, during the protest at Delhi.In the memorandum, the Congress demanded the immediate resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, holding him morally responsible for the alleged irregularities in the paper leak. The party also sought an urgent discussion in Parliament on alleged examination irregularities and issues affecting students' future.The memorandum further demanded that all FIRs and criminal cases registered against students and peaceful protesters be withdrawn immediately.Among those present at the protest were corporator Samina Sheikh, former corporator Iftekar Khan and other Congress office-bearers and workers. Police maintained security at the protest site and ensured traffic movement was restored after the demonstration concluded.
Article Summary: Congress workers staged a rasta roko protest at Shivaji Chowk in Kalyan West. They were protesting against the alleged police action on students demonstrating at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The protesters raised slogans against the Centre and demanded action over the alleged assault on students and peaceful demonstrators.

Article Title: Jantar Mantar violence echoes in KDMC house meet as opposition, MNS protest police action
Article Text:
As soon as the proceedings began, opposition members stood up, shouted slogans and disrupted the House.





KALYAN: The Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation (KDMC) General Body meeting on Thursday witnessed high drama as opposition corporators staged a protest against the alleged police action against students demonstrating at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.Corporators from the opposition, including the Shiv Sena (UBT), Congress and NCP (SP), entered the House carrying the Tricolour and wearing black armbands as a mark of protest. Raising slogans of "Bharat Mata Ki Jai" and "Vande Mataram", they demanded that the House be adjourned to condemn the police action and express solidarity with the injured protesters.As soon as the proceedings began, opposition members stood up, shouted slogans and disrupted the House, forcing Mayor Harshali Chaudhary to adjourn the meeting for 10 minutes.However, after the House reconvened, the opposition continued its protest, condemning what it termed police brutality at Jantar Mantar and urging corporators from the ruling alliance to join them.The protest also witnessed an unusual political alignment, with the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS), a ruling ally of the Shiv Sena in the KDMC, joining hands with the Shiv Sena (UBT) during the demonstration. The BJP took a swipe at the MNS, saying that if MNS corporators wished to sit with the opposition, they should first resign from the ruling alliance and formally move to the opposition benches.Differences within the ruling alliance also came to the fore during the debate. Shiv Sena corporator Mahesh Gaikwad demanded that the House observe a two-minute silence in memory of the students who were allegedly injured in the police action. BJP group leader Shashikant Kamble objected, stating that several police personnel were also injured during the Jantar Mantar protest and that, if a condolence gesture was to be made, it should include them as well.Despite the noisy scenes and repeated slogan-shouting, the General Body meeting continued. Later, leaders of the Shiv Sena and BJP jointly cleared several civic proposals without detailed discussion, while a few agenda items were deferred for consideration at a later meeting.
Article Summary: Corporators from the opposition, including the Shiv Sena (UBT), Congress and NCP (SP), entered the House carrying the Tricolour and wearing black armbands as a mark of protest. Raising slogans of "Bharat Mata Ki Jai" and "Vande Mataram", they demanded that the House be adjourned.

Article Title: Patient’s relative charges at medical practitioner at Sassoon General Hospital
Article Text:
Pune:





A 26-year-old medical practitioner at Sassoon General Hospital has lodged a complaint against a 30-year-old relative of a patient from Ghorpadi, alleging that the man charged at him while he was administering cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) to the patient around 10.40am on Sunday.The Bund Garden police registered a case later that afternoon.According to the FIR, the critically ill patient was brought to the hospital by his relatives.“After examining the patient, the doctor began administering CPR. During the procedure, one of the patient’s relatives started recording the treatment on his cellphone,” an officer from the Bund Garden police said.The doctor, who is pursuing postgraduate studies, asked the relative not to film the CPR procedure.“The relative allegedly began abusing him, leading to an argument. He then charged at the doctor, threatened him with dire consequences, and fled the hospital,” he added.Police have identified the patient’s relative. “Further investigation is underway,” he said.
Article Summary: A 26-year-old medical practitioner at Sassoon General Hospital has lodged a complaint against a relative. The doctor alleges that the man charged at him while he was administering cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) to the patient. Police have identified the patient’s relative.

Article Title: Delivery van driver steals 24 mobile handsets, camera worth Rs 7.71 lakh
Article Text:
Pune:





The Talegaon Dabhade police are searching for the driver of a delivery van attached to an e-commerce company for allegedly fleeing with 24 mobile handsets and a camera collectively worth Rs 7.71 lakh.The owner of the van lodged a complaint with the Talegaon Dabhade police on Saturday.An officer from the Talegaon Dabhade police said the complainant’s van was attached to the e-commerce company for deliveries in the Talegaon Dabhade area.“As per the company’s norms, the vehicle was supposed to make only two stops designated by the company. However, between May 3 and May 30, the driver allegedly made unauthorised stops in the Yashwantnagar area and stole the mobile handsets,” the officer said.He said the theft came to light during an audit. It was found that the driver had stolen 24 mobile handsets and one camera, collectively worth Rs 7.71 lakh, during the period.“We have registered a theft case against the driver. Our investigation is on,” the officer said.
Article Summary: The Talegaon Dabhade police are searching for the driver of a delivery van attached to an e-commerce company for allegedly fleeing with 24 mobile handsets and a camera collectively worth Rs 7.71 lakh. The driver allegedly made unauthorised stops in the Yashwantnagar area.

Article Title: Three arrested for supplying ganja to techies, students in Coimbatore
Article Text:
Representative image





COIMBATORE: The Prohibition Enforcement Wing (PEW) of the Coimbatore city police on Saturday arrested three men for supplying ganja to IT professionals and students here.The arrested have been identified as A Gowtham, 25, of Ganapathy, A Rahul Kumar of Avarampalayam and S Dinesh Kumar, 26, of Kurumapalayam.Acting on specific intelligence about individuals involved in ganja supply to IT professionals and students in the Saravanampatti and Kalapatti neighbourhoods, PEW police led by inspector M Miadit Mano conducted a check near Sungam. They intercepted a car and found ganja in it.Following this, police seized the car and took the trio to the police station for further inquiry, which revealed that they used two more cars and a motorcycle to supply ganja. Police seized three cars, a motorcycle and 4 kg of ganja from them.Police registered a case against them under sections of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. The trio were remanded in judicial custody. Police have initiated a process to freeze their bank accounts.
Article Summary: The Prohibition Enforcement Wing (PEW) of the Coimbatore city police on Saturday arrested three men for supplying ganja to IT professionals and students. The arrested have been identified as A Gowtham, 25, of Ganapathy, A Rahul Kumar of Avarampalayam and S Dinesh Kumar, 26. Police have initiated a process to freeze their bank accounts.

Article Title: Vijay should not go to Karnataka, Anbumani says
Article Text:
Anbumani Ramadoss





CHENNAI: PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss on Friday urged Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay not to hold bilateral talks with his Karnataka counterpart, D K Shivakumar , over the proposed Mekedatu dam.Speaking to reporters, Anbumani said such talks could seriously harm Tamil Nadu’s interests as the lower-riparian state. “Tamil Nadu CM should not go to Karnataka. We should wage both a legal and political battle,” he said.Anbumani called on the chief minister to convene an all-party meeting to decide the future course of action. The chief minister should also lead a delegation of political party leaders, MLAs and MPs to meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Jal Shakti minister C R Patil and register Tamil Nadu’s opposition to the project, he added.
Article Summary: PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss urged Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay not to hold bilateral talks with his Karnataka counterpart, D K Shivakumar. He said such talks could seriously harm Tamil Nadu’s interests as the lower- riparian state.

Article Title: Sengottaiyan flays previous DMK govt for not having pursued legal remedies on Mekedatu dam issue
Article Text:
K A Sengottaiyan





ERODE: Tamil Nadu revenue minister K A Sengottaiyan on Saturday criticized the previous DMK govt for not having pursued legal remedies to stop Karnataka’s move to build a dam across the Cauvery river in Mekedatu.Speaking at a consultation meeting of officials from different departments held at the Erode district collectorate, Sengottaiyan reiterated that chief minister C Joseph Vijay had urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to halt the move to build a dam in Mekedatu.During the review meeting, the minister told officials to deliver results quickly, saying the govt’s performance since coming to power warranted a thorough review and that the people’s demands should be met without delay. “Officers must complete necessary office procedures promptly and ensure citizens receive timely relief,” he told reporters after the meeting.The review, chaired by district collector S Kandasamy and also attended by handloom minister M Vijay Balaji, covered a wide range of administrative concerns.A major focus was the Athikadavu-Avinashi integrated drinking water project. Officials were directed to find out why more than 70 ponds were not getting filled and asked them to take remedial measures. Officials were instructed to begin silt-removal operations in the Bhavanisagar Dam to improve storage capacity and downstream supply.On allegations that liquor outlets were operating in violation of regulations, the revenue minister demanded concrete statistics and warned that strict action would follow where breaches were confirmed.
Article Summary: K A Sengottaiyan criticized the previous DMK govt for not having pursued legal remedies to stop Karnataka’s move to build a dam across the Cauvery river in Mekedatu. He reiterated that chief minister C Joseph Vijay had urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to halt the move.

Article Title: Teen held after 2 schoolboys found dead in well
Article Text:
19-year-old boy on Sunday on charges of murdering two school-going brothers





Theni: Police arrested a 19-year-old boy on Sunday on charges of murdering two school-going brothers by pushing them into a deep well near Bodinayakkanur in Theni district.Police identified the deceased as Sriharis, 11, and Sabareesh, 10, sons of Chinnathambi and Selvi of Renganathapuram near Bodinayakkanur. They were studying in Class VI and V respectively at a govt-aided middle school in the locality.According to Bodinayakkanur rural police, the brothers went missing on Friday evening after school. Based on a complaint filed by their parents, police registered a case and launched a search operation.During the investigation, police examined CCTV footage from a nearby temple where the boys were seen along with Kesava Balaji, 19, a college dropout from the area.They bought and consumed porridge (koozh).When police questioned Balaji, he gave contradictory statements, raising suspicion. Further interrogation revealed that he took the boys to a coconut grove near Muneeswaran Odai at Karattupatti and pushed them into the 150-foot-well.On Saturday evening, fire and rescue personnel retrieved the two bodies, which were sent to Theni Govt Medical College Hospital for postmortem.Balaji was arrested on Sunday and remanded in judicial custody. Police are trying to ascertain the motive behind the crime.
Article Summary: Police identified the deceased as Sriharis, 11, and Sabareesh, 10, sons of Chinnathambi and Selvi of Renganathapuram near Bodinayakkanur. They were studying in Class VI and V respectively at a govt-aided middle school.

Article Title: Unholy nexus between the Congress and CPM in Alappuzha: G Sudhakaran
Article Text:
G Sudhakaran

Kochi:





UDF-backed independent MLA G Sudhakaran, who represents Ambalappuzha segment, alleged that there was an unholy nexus between CPM and Congress in Alappuzha. Sharing dais with home minister Ramesh Chennithala at a function in Alappuzha on Sunday, the communist veteran said the nexus was formed to facilitate corruption and had nothing to do with politics.Sudhakaran said he arrived at the reception organised by the Alappuzha municipality on time a few days ago, and LDF supporters were there to protest against him. Although LDF councillors were holding up placards against him, neither police nor chairperson nor Congress activists took any steps to remove or arrest the protesters. “They had prior knowledge of the move, but they didn’t inform me about that,” Sudhakaran alleged.He said he returned from there thinking that if he attended the event, there would be a law-and-order problem and a riot, and that it would harm the govt. If he had been there, there would have been a fight. “It is my habit to hit back on the cheek if I'm hit,” he said, adding that it was good that he left. He also said that there was a serious lapse on the part of the local police and demanded that Chennithala order an inquiry into the matter.Chennithala said Sudhakaran would be protected and he was a corruption-free minister while holding PWD portfolio twice. Chennithala said that Sudhakaran got a comfortable win in the assembly elections even while he contested as an independent. He also urged the LDF to accept the mandate.
Article Summary: Independent MLA G Sudhakaran alleged that there was an unholy nexus between CPM and Congress in Alappuzha. The communist veteran said the nexus was formed to facilitate corruption and had nothing to do with politics. He said he arrived at the reception on time a few days ago and LDF supporters were there to protest against him.
